submission.natural_language_explanation:
L11/H10 is a page-chrome anchor head: on running prose, a single short line, a plain 'Label: value' list of ordinary words, or a chat turn it keeps its attention on the text's first token (its sink, where the write sits on the 3.07 floor) and peaks at only 0.2-2.3 of its 10.05 maximum, but when the window carries a machine-formatted line - a markup tag or attribute value, a code comment prefix or indentation run, a profile/forum/metadata field row with numeric values ('Posts: 989', 'Joined: 22 Mar 2013', 'Views: 1204'), a citation or reference line, a nav breadcrumb, or blog/forum chrome ('Comments and Sharing', 'Powered by WordPress') - it locks onto one token of that line with attention weight 0.8-1.0, holds it for the rest of the window and copies that token's value into every position, reaching 3-10. It is the lock, not the token it peaks on, that fires it: the peak lands on a delimiter, space or digit inside the locked run ('

', ')

', '-header', ' :', 'Q', '8'), it goes inactive when no token in the window outscores the first-token sink (short word-valued field lists usually do not), and its write promotes no coherent next-token set, so the mechanism is retrospective copying rather than lookahead.

rival_explanations: It is a small-vocabulary token detector rather than a formatting head: it fires wherever one of a fixed set of page-chrome words ('Views', 'Posts', 'Joined', 'Subject', 'Question', ' charset') appears, so a plain prose sentence containing 'Views' should fire just as strongly as a field row, and a well-formed record of other field names should not fire at all.

It is a delimiter/formatting-density head: what drives it is the sheer density of short lines, brackets and markup in the window, so JSON, SQL, a CSS rule block or a markdown table should fire as strongly as HTML attributes or code comments, and long layout-free prose should be the only inactive class.

It is a lookahead copy head: the anchored token is the word the model is about to need next (a repeated field name or template label), so mean-ablating the head should sharply lower the probability of that same token at the following positions.
